verses.text: In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was brought to the king. I picked up the wine and gave it to him. I had never been sad in front of him before.
So the king asked me, "Why do you look so sad? You are not sick. This must be sadness of the heart." I was very afraid,
but I said to the king, "May the king live forever! How can I not look sad? The city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire."
The king asked me, "What do you want?" Then I prayed to the God of heaven.
I answered the king, "If it pleases the king, and if I have pleased you, please send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so that I can rebuild it."
The queen was sitting beside the king. He asked me, "How long will your trip take? When will you come back?" The king was pleased to send me, so I told him how long I would be away.
I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, please give me letters for the governors west of the Euphrates River, so they will let me travel safely until I reach Judah.

Please also give me a letter for Asaph, who is in charge of the king's forest, so he will give me wood. I need it to make beams for the gates of the fortress near the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will live in." The king gave me what I asked for, because my God's kind hand was on me.
So I went to the governors west of the Euphrates River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were very upset that someone had come to help the Israelites.
I arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
Then I got up at night with a few men. I had not told anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one I was riding.
That night I went out through the Valley Gate toward the Jackal Well and the Garbage Gate. I looked at the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and at its gates, which had been burned.
Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was not enough room for my animal to get through.
So I went up the valley that night and looked at the wall. Then I turned back and came in again through the Valley Gate.
The city officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. I had not yet told anything to the Jews, the priests, the important men, the officials, or anyone else who would do the work.
Then I said to them, "You can see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned. Come, let's rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so we will not be ashamed any more."
I told them how my God's kind hand had been on me, and what the king had said to me. They said, "Let's start building!" So they got ready to do this good work.

But when Sanballat from Horon, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they laughed at us and looked down on us. They said, "What are you doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
I answered them, "The God of heaven will give us success. We, his servants, will start building. But you have no share, no right, and no history in Jerusalem."
